# Schema ERD — auto-generated from the migrations, CI-gated against drift (MANDATORY for DB repos)

Every repo that **owns a relational schema** commits a **tbls-generated Mermaid ERD** under
`docs/data-model/` **and** a `schema-erd-drift` CI job that regenerates it from the migrations and
**fails if the committed docs drifted**. The ERD is reverse-engineered from the **same source of truth
as production — the migrations** — never hand-drawn. *"Docs can't lie."* This is the executable form of
the SA **Data design / ERD** artefact (`project-governance.md` #7) and a **Definition-of-Done gate**
(same tier as tests + the as-built doc — `agile-execution.md`, `documentation.md`).

Reusable fact + the full gotcha history: memory `[[reference_tbls_erd_driftcheck]]`. Org doc:
`insurance-platform/schema-erd-autogenerated`.

## Canonical surface — the CENTRAL docs site (one standard, not per-repo sites)
The ERD is **surfaced in exactly one place: the central org docs site** (`minicloud-platform-docs`) —
its **auto-generated ERD index** (`insurance-platform/schema-erd-autogenerated`), where every DB repo's
committed `docs/data-model/README.md` is listed + linked (GitHub renders the Mermaid natively). That index
is produced by **`minicloud-platform-docs/scripts/gen-erd-index.py`** (discovers every repo committing a
`docs/data-model/`, run weekly + on-demand by `update-erd-index.yml`) → **a new DB repo appears with NO
manual step**. Do not hand-maintain the index; do not duplicate the ERD into a per-repo site.

So the **uniform, enforced standard for every DB repo** is exactly three things — identical for all, no
per-service variation:
1. `.tbls.yml` + the committed `docs/data-model/` baseline (or `backend/docs/data-model/` for a monorepo);
2. the `schema-erd-drift` **CI job** (the drift gate);
3. auto-appears on the **central ERD index** (nothing to do — the generator finds it).

A **per-repo `website/` Docusaurus is OPTIONAL** (`conventions.md`) and is NOT the ERD surface. If a repo
*does* have one and wants the diagram in-theme, the only sanctioned way is a **build-time copy** of the
committed `docs/data-model/` into `website/docs/` (never a hand-maintained duplicate) — but the central
index is the standard and is sufficient.

## The CI shape (self-contained — NO live-cluster access)
An ephemeral **Postgres service container** → **apply the repo's migrations** (per toolchain, below) →
run the **digest-pinned tbls** `doc` against it → **`git diff --quiet docs/data-model`** (fail if stale).
Gate the **schema**, built from the migrations, so the doc can never silently rot.

## Materialise the schema — per migration toolchain (all verified)
| Toolchain | Repos | Apply step in CI (+ baseline) |
|---|---|---|
| **Flyway** (raw `V*.sql`) | ktayl-core, ktayl-claims | `psql -f $(ls src/main/resources/db/migration/V*.sql \| sort)` (+ `CREATE SCHEMA`/`SET search_path` if schema-per-module) |
| **golang-migrate** (raw `*.up.sql`) | ktayl-policy-service | `psql -f $(ls db/migrations/*.up.sql \| sort)` |
| **Alembic** (Python) | ktayl-underwriting | `pip install .` → `alembic upgrade head` (reads `DATABASE_URL`) |
| **Drizzle** (raw `*.sql`, drizzle-kit) | retrieva-backend | `psql -f $(ls db/migrations/*.sql \| sort)` (the `--> statement-breakpoint` is a comment → psql-safe) |
| **TypeORM** (TS classes, run on boot) | ktayl-iam | a **standalone `npm run db:migrate`** runner (`DataSource` + `.runMigrations()`, **no app boot** → no HTTP/NATS/OIDC) — NOT `node dist/main` (booting the app drags its deps + may hang) |

## The dbt / warehouse exception — do NOT force tbls (ktayl-data-platform)
A **dbt warehouse** (medallion models materialised FROM live upstream DBs — not a migration-owned schema)
is the **deliberate carve-out**: tbls is the wrong tool. The schema is *derived* (staging views + marts),
so reverse-engineering it would mean standing up source fixtures + a full `dbt build` in CI — heavy and
*lower-value* than dbt's own self-documentation. A dbt repo is already self-documenting and drift-gated by:
- **committed model contracts** (`models/**/_*.yml` — every mart column described + `tests:`), reviewed in-PR;
- **CI `dbt parse`** (offline — validates refs/sources/contracts/macros without a DB connection).
That pair IS the warehouse's "docs-can't-lie" gate. Optionally add `dbt docs generate` (lineage + catalog)
later, but it needs a built warehouse. **Record the carve-out here; don't bolt tbls onto a dbt repo.**

> **TypeORM lesson:** migrations run as a *side-effect of boot* (`migrationsRun: true`). Don't boot the
> whole app in CI to get the schema — write a tiny standalone `DataSource` runner (`src/database/migrate.ts`)
> that only loads the `MIGRATIONS` array. It's a genuinely reusable helper → commit it (`reusable-scripts.md`).

## ⚠️ PIN EVERYTHING or you get false drift (`tbls diff` is byte-exact — cost ~8 CI iterations once)
1. **tbls version** — use the **digest-pinned docker image** `ghcr.io/k1low/tbls@sha256:0d90f07aed0c423a6012d542358c10b13fcdf15a1074ceee3d73676c87cc2f79` via `docker run --network host`. **Do NOT** use `setup-tbls@v1` (installs an old version → SVG defaults → false drift).
2. **Explicit flags, not `.tbls.yml` discovery** — `tbls doc -t mermaid --sort -j` (mermaid = text/deterministic/Docusaurus-renderable). Generate the committed baseline with the **identical** flags.
3. **postgres:17.4** — tbls embeds `database_version` in `schema.json`; pin the service image (matches the CNPG max-PG17 standard) in CI **and** when generating the baseline.
4. **x86_64 baseline** — `database_version` also embeds the CPU arch (`aarch64` vs `x86_64`). Generate the committed baseline on **x86_64** (the controller, or CI itself), **NOT an ARM Mac**, so it matches the x86 runner.
5. **Gate with regenerate + `git diff`** (`tbls doc … --force` then `git diff --quiet -- docs/data-model`), not `tbls diff` (which applies formatting inconsistently across environments).

Net: same tbls (digest) + same pg (17.4) + same arch (x86) + explicit flags → byte-identical regen → clean `git diff`.

## Conventions
- **Location:** `docs/data-model/` at the repo root; for a **monorepo**, under the DB-owning component (e.g. `backend/docs/data-model/` + `backend/.tbls.yml`, running tbls from that dir). Ensure the CI `paths:` filter (if any) covers it.
- **`.tbls.yml`:** `docPath: docs/data-model` · `er.format: mermaid` · `format.sort+adjust: true` · **exclude the migration-bookkeeping table** (`flyway_schema_history` / `public.schema_migrations` / `public.alembic_version` / `public.migrations`).
- **Baseline-generation recipe** (the one-off, on x86): clone the repo → ephemeral `postgres:17.4` → apply the migrations (per toolchain) → native/`docker` digest-pinned tbls `doc … --force` → commit `docs/data-model/` + `.tbls.yml`. Docker-as-root leaves root-owned files in a mounted repo → `chown` back (or generate into a user-owned clone) before `scp`.
- **Reference CI jobs:** copy the `schema-erd-drift` job from `ktayl-core` (Flyway) / `ktayl-policy-service` (golang-migrate) / `ktayl-underwriting` (Alembic) / `ktayl-iam` (TypeORM) / `retrieva-backend` (Drizzle).

## Live DB (adopted / vendor schemas, no migrations in-repo)
For a DB whose schema we **adopted** (vendor app, or no migrations to replay), generate the ERD from the
**live** DB with the reusable generator **`minicloud-ops/scripts/db-erd/generate-erd.sh`** (port-forward +
tbls, creds read from the k8s secret at runtime — no secrets baked). The SSO'd **Adminer** cockpit
(`manifests/adminer/`, `developer-platform/adminer-db-cockpit`) is the Day-2 operational counterpart —
*browse/operate* the DBs; the committed ERD is the *system-of-record documentation*.
